topic: meeting new classmates

grammar_rules:
Tasavvur qiling, Siz yangi ingliz tili guruhidasiz. O‘qituvchi sizdan o‘zingizni tanishtirishingizni so‘raydi. Agar siz (1) kim ekaningizni, (2) qayerdan ekaningizni, (3) yoshingizni, (4) kasbingizni yoki (5) holatingizni aytmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, ingliz tilida ko‘pincha am/is/are ishlatiladi.

Masalan:

I am Ali.
Men Aliman.

I am 18 years old.
Men 18 yoshdaman.

I am from Uzbekistan.
Men O‘zbekistondanman.

I am a student.
Men talabaman.

My name is Ali.
Mening ismim Ali.

Subject pronouns — gapda ish-harakatni bajaruvchi yoki kim/nima haqida gap ketayotganini bildiruvchi olmoshlar.

Oddiy qilib:

Subject pronoun = gap kim haqida ekanini bildiradi.

Masalan:

I am Ali.
Bu gap men haqimda.

She is my sister.
Bu gap u qiz/ayol haqida.

They are students.
Bu gap ular haqida.

English | O‘zbekcha | Qachon ishlatiladi?
I | Men | O‘zingiz haqida
You | Sen/siz | suhbatdoshingiz haqida
He | U | erkak / o‘g‘il bola haqida
She | U | ayol / qiz haqida
It | U/bu | narsa, hayvon, joy, ob-havo haqida
We | Biz | o‘zingiz va boshqalar haqida
They | Ular | o‘zingiz va boshqalar haqida

O‘zbek tilida ko‘pincha ega tushib qoladi:

Men talabaman deyish mumkin.
Ba’zan shunchaki Talabaman ham deyiladi.

Lekin ingliz tilida odatda ega kerak:

I am a student.

Faqat am a student deyilmaydi.

Shuning uchun Ingliz tilida gap boshida “kim?” aniq bo‘lishi kerak.

I am...
You are...
He is...
She is...
We are...
They are...

Agar siz biror narsa sizga tegishli ekanini aytmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, ingliz tilida my ishlatasiz.

My name — mening ismim
My family — mening oilam
My city — mening shahrim
My hobby — mening qiziqishim
My goal — mening maqsadim

Masalan:

My name is Ali.
Mening ismim Ali.

My city is Urgench.
Mening shahrim Urganch.

My hobby is reading.
Mening qiziqishim kitob o‘qish.

My goal is to become a doctor.
Mening maqsadim shifokor bo‘lish.

Yana bir misol:

Hello. My name is Madina. — Salom. Mening ismim Madina.
I am 17 years old. — Men 17 yoshdaman.
I am from Urgench. — Men Urganchdanman.
I am a student. — Men o‘quvchiman/talabaman.
My hobby is reading. — Mening qiziqishim kitob o‘qish.
My goal is to speak English fluently. — Mening maqsadim ingliz tilida ravon gapirish.
grammar_rules_en:
Imagine you are in a new English class. The teacher asks you to introduce yourself. If you want to say (1) who you are, (2) where you are from, (3) how old you are, (4) what you do or (5) how you are, English usually uses am/is/are.

For example:

I am Ali.

I am 18 years old.

I am from Uzbekistan.

I am a student.

My name is Ali.

Subject pronouns are pronouns that show who does the action in a sentence, or who/what the sentence is about.

In simple terms:

Subject pronoun = shows who the sentence is about.

For example:

I am Ali.
This sentence is about me.

She is my sister.
This sentence is about her.

They are students.
This sentence is about them.

English | Uzbek | When to use?
I | Men | About yourself
You | Sen/siz | About your conversation partner
He | U | About a man/boy
She | U | About a woman/girl
It | U/bu | About a thing, animal, place, weather
We | Biz | About yourself and others
They | Ular | About yourself and others

In Uzbek, the subject is often omitted:

You can say Men talabaman.
Sometimes it is simply said as Talabaman.

But in English, the subject is usually needed:

I am a student.

You cannot just say am a student.

Therefore, in English, it must be clear "who?" at the beginning of the sentence.

I am...
You are...
He is...
She is...
We are...
They are...

If you want to say that something belongs to you, you use my in English.

My name
My family
My city
My hobby
My goal

For example:

My name is Ali.

My city is Urgench.

My hobby is reading.

My goal is to become a doctor.

Another example:

Hello. My name is Madina. — Salom. Mening ismim Madina.
I am 17 years old. — Men 17 yoshdaman.
I am from Urgench. — Men Urganchdanman.
I am a student. — Men o‘quvchiman/talabaman.
My hobby is reading. — Mening qiziqishim kitob o‘qish.
My goal is to speak English fluently. — Mening maqsadim ingliz tilida ravon gapirish.
grammar_rules_ru:
Представьте, что вы в новой группе английского языка. Преподаватель просит вас представиться. Если вы (1) кто вы, (2) откуда вы, (3) сколько вам лет, (4) кем вы работаете или (5) как вы себя чувствуете, в английском обычно используются am/is/are.

Например:

I am Ali.
Я Али.

I am 18 years old.
Мне 18 лет.

I am from Uzbekistan.
Я из Узбекистана.

I am a student.
Я студент.

My name is Ali.
Меня зовут Али.

Subject pronouns — местоимения, которые обозначают в предложении того, кто выполняет действие, или того, о ком/о чём идёт речь.

Простыми словами:

Subject pronoun = местоимение, которое указывает, о ком идет речь в предложении.

Например:

I am Ali.
Это предложение обо мне.

She is my sister.
Это предложение о ней, девушке/женщине.

They are students.
Это предложение об них.

English | O‘zbekcha | Когда используется?
I | Men | О себе
You | Sen/siz | О собеседнике
He | U | О мужчине / мальчике
She | U | О женщине / девушке
It | U/bu | О предмете, животном, месте, погоде
We | Biz | О себе и других
They | Ular | О себе и других

В узбекском языке часто подлежащее опускается:

Можно сказать Men talabaman. 
Иногда просто Talabaman тоже говорят.

Но в английском языке обычно подлежащее нужно:

I am a student.

Не говорят просто am a student.

Поэтому в английском языке в начале предложения должно быть ясно "кто?:"

I am...
You are...
He is...
She is...
We are...
They are...

Если вы хотите сказать, что что-то принадлежит вам, в английском языке используется my.

My name — моё имя
My family — моя семья
My city — мой город
My hobby — моё хобби
My goal — моя цель

Например:

My name is Ali.
Меня зовут Али.

My city is Urgench.
Мой город Ургенч.

My hobby is reading.
Моё хобби — чтение.

My goal is to become a doctor.
Моя цель — стать врачом.

Ещё один пример:

Hello. My name is Madina. — Привет. Меня зовут Мадина.
I am 17 years old. — Мне 17 лет.
I am from Urgench. — Я из Ургенча.
I am a student. — Я студент.
My hobby is reading. — Моё хобби — чтение.
My goal is to speak English fluently. — Моя цель — говорить по-английски свободно.

Subject pronouns — gápte is-háreketti orınlawshını yamasa kim/ne haqqında gáp bolıp atırǵanın bildiretuǵın almasıqlar.

Subject pronoun = gáp kim haqqında ekenin bildiredi.

They are students.
Bu gáp ular haqqında.

English | Qaraqalpaq | Qayda qollanıladı?
I | Men | Ózińiz haqqında
You | Sen/siz | suhbatdoshińız haqqında
He | U | erkek / oǵıl bola haqqında
She | U | ayol / qız haqqında
It | U/bu | narsa, haywan, joy, ob-háwa haqqında

I am...

Eger siz biror narsa sizge tegishli ekenin aytmaqshı bolsańız, ingliz tilinde my qollanasız.

reading_passage:
Maya is taking part in a lesson about meeting new classmates. The activity is set in a university orientation desk.

Maya is from Urgench and studies information technology. Daniel is from Nukus and is nineteen years old.

The students receive name cards before entering the classroom. The orientation leader asks everyone to introduce themselves in one short sentence.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “I am Maya, Daniel is my classmate, and we are ready.” By the end, both students remember each other’s names and feel more comfortable.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Maya explains the main idea to Daniel and supports the answer with information from the text.

The final task asks readers to connect the topic with their own experience. They should explain one idea in their own words and then use the lesson grammar in a new sentence about meeting new classmates.

title: A world of sport
grammar_focus: To be: negatives, questions & short answers
topic: joining an international sports club

grammar_rules:
Bu darsda siz am, is, are yordamida inkor gap va savol gap tuzishni o‘rganasiz.

Siz yangi ingliz tili guruhidasiz. O‘qituvchi siz bilan tanishmoqda. U sizdan savollar so‘raydi:

Are you a student?
Siz talabamisiz?

Are you from Urgench?
Siz Urganchdanmisiz?

Are you tired?
Siz charchadingizmi?

Siz esa ba’zan “ha”, ba’zan “yo‘q” deb javob berasiz:

Yes, I am.
Ha.

No, I am not.
Yo‘q.

Bu dars hayotda juda kerak bo‘ladigan oddiy savol-javoblarni o‘rgatadi.

To be ingliz tilida “bo‘lmoq” ma’nosida keladi. Hozirgi zamonda uning 3 ta shakli bor:

I – am

He/she/it – is

We/you/they – are

Misollar:

I am a student.
Men talabaman.

He is my friend.
U mening do‘stim.

They are classmates.
Ular sinfdoshlar.

Negative form — inkor gap. Ya’ni biror narsaning to‘g‘ri emasligini aytish uchun ishlatiladi.

O‘zbek tilida:

Men o‘qituvchi emasman.
U mening akam emas.
Ular kechikmagan.

Ingliz tilida inkor qilish uchun am / is / are dan keyin not qo‘yiladi.

Positive | Negative
I am a student. | I am not a teacher.
You are my friend. | You are not my brother.
He is from Urgench. | He is not from Tashkent.
She is my classmate. | She is not my sister.
It is my book. | It is not my phone.
We are students. | We are not teachers.
They are classmates. | They are not relatives.

Ingliz tilida og‘zaki nutqda qisqa shakllar ko‘p ishlatiladi.

Full form | Short form
I am not | I’m not
You are not | You aren’t
He is not | He isn’t
She is not | She isn’t
It is not | It isn’t
We are not | We aren’t
They are not | They aren’t

Misollar:

I’m not a teacher.
Men o‘qituvchi emasman.

He isn’t my friend.
U mening do‘stim emas.

They aren’t late.
Ular kechikmagan.

Question form — savol gap. Ya’ni biror narsani so‘rash uchun ishlatiladi.

O‘zbek tilida:

Siz talabamisiz?
U sizning do‘stingizmi?
Ular kechikdimi?

Ingliz tilida to be bilan savol qilish uchun am / is / are gap boshiga chiqadi.

You are a student.
Siz talabasisiz.

Question sentence

Are you a student?
Siz talabamisiz?

Demak, savol qilish uchun are oldinga chiqdi.

Positive | Question
I am late. | Am I late?
You are a student. | Are you a student?
He is your friend. | Is he your friend?
She is from Urgench. | Is she from Urgench?
It is your book. | Is it your book?
We are classmates. | Are we classmates?
They are students. | Are they students?

Question | Positive answer | Negative answer
Are you a student? | Yes, I am. | No, I am not.
Is he your friend? | Yes, he is. | No, he is not.
Is she from Urgench? | Yes, she is. | No, she is not.
Is it your book? | Yes, it is. | No, it is not.
Are we late? | Yes, we are. | No, we are not.
Are they students? | Yes, they are. | No, they are not.

O‘zbek tilida savol qilish uchun ko‘pincha -mi qo‘shimchasi ishlatiladi:

Siz talabamisiz?
U o‘qituvchimi?

Ingliz tilida esa am / is / are oldinga chiqadi:

Are you a student?
Is he a teacher?

Shuning uchun savol qilishda tartib juda muhim.

Teacher: Are you a student?
Student: Yes, I am.

Teacher: Are you from Tashkent?
Student: No, I am not. I am from Urgench.

Teacher: Is Ali your friend?
Student: Yes, he is.

Teacher: Is Madina your sister?
Student: No, she is not. She is my classmate.

Teacher: Are they your classmates?
Student: Yes, they are.
grammar_rules_en:
In this lesson you will learn to make negative sentences and questions with am, is and are.

You are in a new English class. The teacher is getting to know you and asks you some questions:

Are you a student?

Are you from Urgench?

Are you tired?

Sometimes you answer “yes”, and sometimes “no”:

Yes, I am.

No, I am not.

This lesson teaches simple questions and answers that are very necessary in life.

To be means “to be” in English. In the present tense, it has 3 forms:

I – am

He/she/it – is

We/you/they – are

Examples:

I am a student.

He is my friend.

They are classmates.

Negative form — a negative sentence. It is used to say that something is not true.

In Uzbek:

I am not a teacher.
He is not my brother.
They are not late.

In English, to make a negative, not is added after am / is / are.

Positive | Negative
I am a student. | I am not a teacher.
You are my friend. | You are not my brother.
He is from Urgench. | He is not from Tashkent.
She is my classmate. | She is not my sister.
It is my book. | It is not my phone.
We are students. | We are not teachers.
They are classmates. | They are not relatives.

In spoken English, short forms are often used.

Full form | Short form
I am not | I’m not
You are not | You aren’t
He is not | He isn’t
She is not | She isn’t
It is not | It isn’t
We are not | We aren’t

A university English class is exploring joining an international sports club through a short article set in the campus sports centre.

The club offers football, volleyball, swimming and table tennis. New members answer simple questions about where they are from and which sport they like.

Sara is not a professional athlete but she is an enthusiastic volleyball player. The coach checks whether students are free for training on Tuesday evenings.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “Are you ready, Leo? No, I am not nervous; I am ready.” Sara joins the volleyball group and receives the training schedule.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Sara explains the main idea to Leo and supports the answer with information from the text.

The final task asks readers to connect the topic with their own experience. They should explain one idea in their own words and then use the lesson grammar in a new sentence about joining an international sports club.

grammar_rules:
1. Subject + Verb + Object (Word order (so‘z tartibi), Positive / Negative / Question)

Word Order — Ingliz tilida so‘z tartibi

Siz bilan ingliz tilida gap tuzishni o‘rganamiz. Ingliz tilida gap tuzishda eng muhim narsalardan biri bu so‘z tartibi. O‘zbek tilida so‘zlarning joyi biroz erkinroq bo‘lishi mumkin, lekin ingliz tilida gapdagi so‘zlar aniq tartibda keladi. Masalan, o‘zbek tilida “Men ingliz tilini o‘rganaman” deymiz. Ingliz tilida esa bu gap I study English bo‘ladi. Ya’ni ingliz tilida odatda avval kim?, keyin nima qiladi?, undan keyin nimani? keladi. Shuning uchun inglizcha gap tuzishda eng asosiy formula:

Subject + Verb + Object, ya’ni Ega + Fe’l + To‘ldiruvchi.

Bu mavzu kundalik hayotda juda ko‘p ishlatiladi. Siz o‘zingiz haqingizda gapirmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, do‘stingizni tanishtirsangiz, nimani yoqtirishingizni aytsangiz yoki biror ish-harakatni tushuntirsangiz, word order kerak bo‘ladi. Masalan: I like music — “Men musiqani yoqtiraman”, She reads books — “U kitoblar o‘qiydi”, They play football — “Ular futbol o‘ynaydi”. Bu gaplarda tartib bir xil: avval subject, keyin verb, keyin object kelgan.

Ingliz tilida oddiy darak gaplarda ko‘pincha formula shunday bo‘ladi: Subject + Verb + Object. Masalan, I watch movies, We learn English, Ali plays chess. Bu gaplarda I, we, Ali — subject, watch, learn, plays — verb, movies, English, chess — object. O‘zbek talabalari ko‘p qiladigan xato shuki, ular o‘zbekcha tartibni inglizchaga ko‘chiradi. Masalan, I English learn deyishadi. Bu noto‘g‘ri. To‘g‘ri shakli: I learn English.

So‘roq gaplarda esa so‘z tartibi o‘zgaradi. Yordamchi fe’llar savol berilganda gap boshiga chiqadi. Masalan, She is a teacher darak gap bo‘lsa, savol shakli Is she a teacher? bo‘ladi. They are ready gapining savol shakli Are they ready?bo‘ladi.

Inkor gaplarda ham zamonga qarab so‘z tartibi o‘zgaradi. Yordamchi fe’lga not qo‘shish orqali ishlatiladi: I don’t drink coffee, She doesn’t like tea, They don’t watch TV, I am not tired, She is not at home, They are not ready.

Demak, ingliz tilida so‘z tartibi gapning turiga va zamoniga qarab o‘zgaradi, lekin asosiy fikr bitta: ingliz tilida so‘zlar tartibsiz joylashmaydi. Darak gaplarda odatda avval subject, keyin verb, keyin esa object yoki complement keladi. Savol gaplarda yordamchi fe’l yoki to be/modal verb ko‘pincha gap boshiga chiqadi. Inkor gaplarda esa not, don’t/doesn’t, didn’t, won’t kabi so‘zlar ishlatiladi.
grammar_rules_en:
1. Subject + Verb + Object (Word order, Positive / Negative / Question)

Word Order — Word order in English

We will learn how to build sentences in English. One of the most important things when building an English sentence is word order. In Uzbek, words can move around a little more freely, but in English the words of a sentence come in a fixed order. For example, in Uzbek we say “Men ingliz tilini o‘rganaman”. In English this sentence is I study English. In other words, English usually puts who? first, then does what?, and then what? That is why the basic formula for an English sentence is:

Subject + Verb + Object, that is, Subject + Verb + Object.

This topic comes up all the time in everyday life. When you want to talk about yourself, introduce a friend, say what you like or explain an action, you need word order. For example: I like music — “Men musiqani yoqtiraman”, She reads books — “U kitoblar o‘qiydi”, They play football — “Ular futbol o‘ynaydi”. The order in these sentences is the same: first the subject, then the verb, then the object.

In simple English statements the formula is usually: Subject + Verb + Object. For example, I watch movies, We learn English, Ali plays chess. In these sentences I, we and Ali are the subjects; watch, learn and plays are the verbs; movies, English and chess are the objects. A common mistake Uzbek students make is carrying Uzbek word order into English. For example, they say I English learn. This is wrong. The correct form is: I learn English.

In question sentences, the word order changes. Auxiliary verbs move to the beginning of the sentence when asking a question. For example, She is a teacher is a statement, while the question form is Is she a teacher? The question form of They are ready is Are they ready?

In negative sentences, the word order also changes depending on the tense. It is used by adding not to the auxiliary verb: I don’t drink coffee, She doesn’t like tea, They don’t watch TV, I am not tired, She is not at home, They are not ready.

Thus, in English, word order changes according to the type of sentence and tense, but the main idea is the same: in English, words do not appear in a random order. In affirmative sentences, the usual order is subject first, then verb, and then object or complement. In question sentences, the auxiliary verb or to be/modal verb often moves to the beginning of the sentence. In negative sentences, words like not, don’t/doesn’t, didn’t, won’t are used.
grammar_rules_ru:
1. Subject + Verb + Object (Word order (порядок слов), Positive / Negative / Question)

Word Order — Порядок слов в английском языке

Мы с вами будем учиться строить предложения на английском. Одной из самых важных вещей при построении английского предложения является порядок слов. В узбекском языке слова могут стоять более свободно, но в английском слова в предложении идут в строгом порядке. Например, по-узбекски мы говорим «Men ingliz tilini o‘rganaman». По-английски же это предложение звучит как I study English. То есть в английском обычно сначала идёт кто?, затем что делает?, а потом что? Поэтому основная формула английского предложения:

Subject + Verb + Object, то есть Подлежащее + Сказуемое + Дополнение.

Эта тема очень часто встречается в повседневной жизни. Когда вы хотите рассказать о себе, представить друга, сказать, что вам нравится, или объяснить какое-то действие, вам нужен word order. Например: I like music — «Я люблю музыку», She reads books — «Она читает книги», They play football — «Они играют в футбол». Порядок в этих предложениях одинаковый: сначала subject, затем verb, затем object.

В простых утвердительных предложениях формула обычно такая: Subject + Verb + Object. Например, I watch movies, We learn English, Ali plays chess. В этих предложениях I, we, Ali — subject; watch, learn, plays — verb; movies, English, chess — object. Частая ошибка узбекских студентов заключается в том, что они переносят узбекский порядок слов в английский. Например, говорят I English learn.

В вопросительных предложениях порядок слов меняется. Вспомогательные глаголы при задавании вопроса выходят на первое место. Например, She is a teacher — это утвердительное предложение, а в вопросительной форме будет Is she a teacher? Вопросительная форма предложения They are ready будет Are they ready?

В отрицательных предложениях также в зависимости от времени порядок слов меняется. Используется вспомогательный глагол с частицей not: I don’t drink coffee, She doesn’t like tea, They don’t watch TV, I am not tired, She is not at home, They are not ready.

Таким образом, в английском языке порядок слов меняется в зависимости от типа и времени предложения, но основная идея одна: в английском языке слова не располагаются беспорядочно. В утвердительных предложениях обычно сначала subject, затем verb, а затем object или complement. В вопросительных предложениях вспомогательный глагол или to be/modal verb часто выходит на первое место. В отрицательных предложениях используются такие слова, как not, don’t/doesn’t, didn’t, won’t.
grammar_rules_kk:
1. Subject + Verb + Object (Word order (sózler tártibi), Positive / Negative / Question)

Word Order — inglis tilinde sózler tártibi

Siz bilen inglis tilinde gáp dúziwdi úyrenemiz. Inglis tilinde gáp dúziwde eń áhmiyetli nárselerdiń biri bul sózler tártibi. Ózbek tilinde sózlardıń orını birqansha erkinirek bolıwı múmkin, biraq inglis tilinde gáptegi sózlar anıq tártip penen keledi. Mısalı, ózbek tilinde “Men inglis tilin úyrenamen” deymiz. Al inglis tilinde bul gáp I study English boladı. Yaǵnıy inglis tilinde ádette aldı kim?, keyin ne isleydi?, onnan keyin neni? keledi. Sonlıqtan inglisshe gáp dúziwdiń eń tiykarǵı formulası:

Subject + Verb + Object, yaǵnıy Baslawısh + Feyil + Tolıqlawısh.

Bul tema kúndelikli turmısta júdá kóp qollanıladı. Siz ózińiz haqqında aytpaqshı bolsańız, dosıńızdı tanıstırsańız, neni unatatuǵınıńızdı aytsańız yamasa qanday da bir is-háreketti túsindirseńiz, word order kerek boladı. Mısalı: I like music — “Men muzıkanı unataman”, She reads books — “Ol kitaplar oqıydı”, They play football — “Olar futbol oynaydı”. Bul gáplerde tártip birdey: aldı menen subject, keyin verb, keyin object kelgen.

Inglis tilinde ápiwayı darak gáplerde kóbinese formula usınday boladı: Subject + Verb + Object. Mısalı, I watch movies, We learn English, Ali plays chess. Bul gáplerde I, we, Ali — subject; watch, learn, plays — verb; movies, English, chess — object. Ózbek talabalari kóp jiberetuǵın qáte — óz tilindegi tártipti inglis tiline kóshiriw. Mısalı, I English learn deyishadi. Bul notoǵrı. Toǵrı shaklı: I learn English.

So‘roq gáplerde esa sóz tártibi ózgaradı. Yordamçı feyller savol berilgande gáp boshına şıǵadı. Mısalı, She is a teacher darak gáp bolǵanda, savol shaklı Is she a teacher? boladı. They are ready gápınıń savol shaklı Are they ready? boladı.

Inkor gáplerde hám zamonga qarap sóz tártibi ózgaradı. Yordamçı feylga not qo‘shıw arqılı qollanıladı: I don’t drink coffee, She doesn’t like tea, They don’t watch TV, I am not tired, She is not at home, They are not ready.

Demak, ingliz tilinde sóz tártibi gápnyń turına hám zamonına qarap ózgaradı, lekin asosiy fikr bitta: ingliz tilinde sózlar tartibsiz joylaşmaydı. Darak gáplerde odatda avval subject, keyin verb, keyin esa object yoki complement keladi. Savol gáplerde yordamçı feyl yoki to be/modal verb kópına gáp boshına şıǵadı. Inkor gáplerde esa not, don’t/doesn’t, didn’t, won’t kabi sózlar qollanıladı.

Hi Adam,

Today our English class worked on how students use digital tools. The example came from a university digital skills workshop.

Students use cloud documents to share notes instead of sending many separate files. Nina checks university messages on her phone every morning.

The teacher warns students to keep sentences clear when giving instructions to AI tools. The group compares a confusing message with a version that follows normal English word order.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “I use my laptop every day for study.” The class creates a short digital-study guide for first-year students.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Nina explains the main idea to Adam and supports the answer with information from the text.

The final task asks readers to connect the topic with their own experience. They should explain one idea in their own words and then use the lesson grammar in a new sentence about how students use digital tools.

grammar_rules:
Ingliz tilida pronoun, ya’ni olmosh, otning o‘rnida ishlatiladigan so‘zdir. Masalan, har safar Ali, Ali, Ali deb takrorlash o‘rniga, biz he deymiz. This is Ali. Ali is my friend. Ali is a student deyish o‘rniga, tabiiyroq qilib: This is Ali. He is my friend. He is a student deymiz. Demak, olmoshlar gapni qisqaroq, chiroyliroq va takrorsiz qilish uchun kerak. Ingliz tilida olmoshlar juda muhim, chunki ular gapda kim haqida gap ketayotganini, narsa kimga tegishli ekanini yoki ish-harakat kimning o‘ziga qaratilganini bildiradi. Eng ko‘p ishlatiladigan olmosh turlari: personal pronouns — kishilik olmoshlari, possessive pronouns / possessive adjectives — egalik olmoshlari va reflexive pronouns — o‘zlik olmoshlaridir.

Personal pronouns, ya’ni kishilik olmoshlari, shaxs yoki narsani bildiradi. Ular gapda ega yoki to‘ldiruvchi bo‘lib kelishi mumkin. Ega bo‘lib kelganda: I, you, he, she, it, we, they ishlatiladi. Masalan:

I am a student — Men talabaman.
You are my friend — Sen mening do‘stimsan.
He is a teacher — U erkak kishi o‘qituvchi.
She is a doctor — U ayol kishi shifokor.
It is a book — Bu kitob.
We are students — Biz talabamiz.
They are teachers — Ular o‘qituvchilar.

Bu yerda olmoshlar gapning boshida kelib, ish-harakatni bajarayotgan shaxs yoki narsani bildiradi. Ingliz tilida he erkak kishi uchun, she ayol kishi uchun, it esa hayvon, narsa, predmet yoki mavhum tushunchalar uchun ishlatiladi. Masalan: This is my phone. It is new — Bu mening telefonim. U yangi.

Kishilik olmoshlari gapda to‘ldiruvchi bo‘lib kelganda shakli o‘zgaradi: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Masalan:

She helps me — U menga yordam beradi.
I know him — Men uni taniyman.
We love her — Biz uni yaxshi ko‘ramiz.
Teacher asked us — O‘qituvchi bizdan so‘radi.
I saw them yesterday — Men ularni kecha ko‘rdim.

Bu yerda me, him, her, us, them ish-harakatni bajarmaydi, aksincha ish-harakat ularga qaratilgan bo‘ladi. Shuning uchun I saw he deyish noto‘g‘ri, to‘g‘risi: I saw him. She called I ham noto‘g‘ri, to‘g‘risi: She called me.

Possessive adjectives va possessive pronouns, ya’ni egalikni bildiruvchi olmoshlar, biror narsa kimga tegishli ekanini ko‘rsatadi. Ingliz tilida egalikni bildirishning ikki ko‘rinishi bor. Birinchisi ot bilan birga ishlatiladi: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Masalan:

my book — mening kitobim,
your pen — sening ruchkang,
his car — uning mashinasi,
her bag— uning sumkasi,
our school — bizning maktabimiz,
their house — ularning uyi.

Bu so‘zlardan keyin albatta ot keladi. Masalan: This is my book — Bu mening kitobim. Her English is good — Uning ingliz tili yaxshi. Their teacher is very kind — Ularning o‘qituvchisi juda mehribon.

Ikkinchi ko‘rinishi esa otning o‘rnida mustaqil ishlatiladi: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Masalan:

This book is mine — Bu kitob meniki.
That pen is yours — Ana u ruchka seniki.
This car is his — Bu mashina uniki.
The red bag is hers — Qizil sumka uniki.
This classroom is ours — Bu sinfxona bizniki.
That house is theirs — Ana u uy ularniki.

Bu yerda olmoshdan keyin ot kelmaydi, chunki ot avval aytilgan yoki ma’nodan tushunarli bo‘ladi. Masalan, This is my book. That is yours — Bu mening kitobim. Ana unisi seniki. Bu gapda yours so‘zi your book o‘rnida ishlatilgan.

Reflexive pronouns, ya’ni o‘zlik olmoshlari, ish-harakat bajaruvchining o‘ziga qaytishini bildiradi. Ular: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Masalan:

I taught myself English — Men ingliz tilini o‘zim o‘rgandim.
She looked at herself in the mirror — U oynada o‘ziga qaradi.
He hurt himself — U o‘zini jarohatlab oldi.
We prepared ourselves for the exam — Biz imtihonga o‘zimizni tayyorladik.
They introduced themselves— Ular o‘zlarini tanishtirishdi.

O‘zlik olmoshlari “o‘zim, o‘zing, o‘zi, o‘zimiz, o‘zlari” ma’nosini beradi. Bu olmoshlar ayniqsa ish-harakat boshqa odamga emas, aynan bajaruvchining o‘ziga qaratilganini ko‘rsatadi.

O‘zlik olmoshlari ba’zan ta’kidlash uchun ham ishlatiladi. Masalan:

I did it myself — Men buni o‘zim qildim.

Bu gapda “boshqa odam emas, aynan men qildim” degan ma’no bor.

The director himself came to the meeting — Direktorning o‘zi majlisga keldi.
She herself cooked the dinner — Ovqatni uning o‘zi pishirdi.

Bunday holatda o‘zlik olmoshi ish-harakatni kuchliroq ta’kidlaydi va gapga ishonchliroq ohang beradi.

Quyidagi misollar olmoshlarning farqini yaxshiroq tushunishga yordam beradi:

I am a student — bu yerda I kishilik olmoshi, ega vazifasida kelgan.
Teacher helped me — bu yerda me kishilik olmoshi, to‘ldiruvchi vazifasida kelgan.
This is my notebook — bu yerda my egalikni bildiradi va undan keyin ot kelgan.
This notebook is mine — bu yerda mine “meniki” degan ma’noda mustaqil ishlatilgan.
I bought it myself — bu yerda myself “o‘zim” degan ma’noda ishlatilgan.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, pronouns ingliz tilida otlarning o‘rnida kelib, gapni takrorsiz va tabiiy qiladi. Personal pronouns shaxs yoki narsani bildiradi: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Ularning to‘ldiruvchi shakllari: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Possessive adjectives narsa kimga tegishli ekanini ot bilan birga ko‘rsatadi: my book, your pen, his car, her bag. Possessive pronouns esa “meniki, seniki, uniki, bizniki, ularniki” ma’nosida mustaqil ishlatiladi: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Reflexive pronouns esa “o‘zim, o‘zing, o‘zi, o‘zimiz, o‘zlari” ma’nosini bildiradi: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Bu olmoshlarni to‘g‘ri ishlatish ingliz tilida ravon, aniq va chiroyli gapirish uchun juda muhim.
grammar_rules_en:
In English, a pronoun is a word used in place of a noun. For example, instead of repeating Ali, Ali, Ali every time, we say he. Instead of saying This is Ali. Ali is my friend. Ali is a student, we say it more naturally: This is Ali. He is my friend. He is a student. So pronouns make sentences shorter, nicer and free of repetition. Pronouns are very important in English, because they show who the sentence is about, whom something belongs to, or whether an action is directed back at the person doing it. The most common types are: personal pronouns — kishilik olmoshlari, possessive pronouns / possessive adjectives — egalik olmoshlari va reflexive pronouns — o‘zlik olmoshlaridir.

Personal pronouns, ya’ni kishilik olmoshlari, shaxs yoki narsani bildiradi. Ular gapda ega yoki to‘ldiruvchi bo‘lib kelishi mumkin. Ega bo‘lib kelganda: I, you, he, she, it, we, they ishlatiladi. Masalan:

I am a student.
You are my friend.
He is a teacher.
She is a doctor.
It is a book.
We are students.
They are teachers.

Here the pronouns come at the start of the sentence and show the person or thing doing the action. In English, he is used for a man, she for a woman, and it for animals, things, objects or abstract ideas. For example: This is my phone. It is new.

When personal pronouns are used as objects in a sentence, their form changes: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. For example:

She helps me.
I know him.
We love her.
Teacher asked us.
I saw them yesterday.

Here me, him, her, us, them do not perform the action; rather, the action is directed towards them. Therefore, saying I saw he is incorrect; the correct form is: I saw him. Saying She called I is also incorrect; the correct form is: She called me.

Possessive adjectives and possessive pronouns, ya’ni egalikni bildiruvchi olmoshlar, biror narsa kimga tegishli ekanini ko‘rsatadi. Ingliz tilida egalikni bildirishning ikki ko‘rinishi bor. Birinchisi ot bilan birga ishlatiladi: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Masalan:

my book — mening kitobim,
your pen — sening ruchkang,
his car — uning mashinasi,
her bag— uning sumkasi,
our school — bizning maktabimiz,
their house — ularning uyi.

These words are always followed by a noun. For example: This is my book — Bu mening kitobim. Her English is good — Uning ingliz tili yaxshi. Their teacher is very kind — Ularning o‘qituvchisi juda mehribon.

The second form is used independently instead of a noun: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. For example:

This book is mine.
That pen is yours.
This car is his.
The red bag is hers.
This classroom is ours.
That house is theirs.

Here, there is no noun after the pronoun, because the noun has already been mentioned or is clear from the context. For example, This is my book. That is yours — Bu mening kitobim. Ana unisi seniki. In this sentence, the word yours is used instead of your book.

Reflexive pronouns, ya’ni o‘zlik olmoshlari, ish-harakat bajaruvchining o‘ziga qaytishini bildiradi. Ular: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Masalan:

I taught myself English.
She looked at herself in the mirror.
He hurt himself.
We prepared ourselves for the exam.
They introduced themselves.

Reflexive pronouns mean “o‘zim, o‘zing, o‘zi, o‘zimiz, o‘zlari”. These pronouns especially indicate that the action is directed towards the performer themselves, not another person.

Reflexive pronouns are sometimes used for emphasis. For example:

I did it myself.

This sentence means “not someone else, but I did it.”

The director himself came to the meeting.
She herself cooked the dinner.

In such cases, the reflexive pronoun emphasizes the action more strongly and gives the sentence a more confident tone.

The following examples help to better understand the difference between pronouns:

I am a student — here I is a personal pronoun, used as a subject.
Teacher helped me — here me is a personal pronoun, used as an object.
This is my notebook — here my indicates possession and is followed by a noun.
This notebook is mine — here mine is used independently in the sense of “meniki.”
I bought it myself — here myself is used in the sense of “o‘zim.”

In conclusion, pronouns in English come in place of nouns, making sentences concise and natural. Personal pronouns refer to a person or thing: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Their object forms are: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Possessive adjectives indicate to whom something belongs along with the noun: my book, your pen, his car, her bag. Possessive pronouns are used independently with the meaning of “mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs”: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Reflexive pronouns express the meaning of “myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves”: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Using these pronouns correctly is very important for speaking English fluently, clearly, and beautifully.
grammar_rules_ru:
В английском языке pronoun, то есть местоимение, — это слово, которое используется вместо существительного. Например, вместо того чтобы каждый раз повторять Ali, Ali, Ali, мы говорим he. Вместо This is Ali. Ali is my friend. Ali is a student естественнее сказать: This is Ali. He is my friend. He is a student. Значит, местоимения нужны, чтобы сделать речь короче, красивее и без повторов. Местоимения в английском очень важны, потому что они показывают, о ком идёт речь, кому принадлежит предмет или направлено ли действие на самого себя. Самые распространённые виды местоимений: personal pronouns — личные местоимения, possessive pronouns / possessive adjectives — притяжательные местоимения и reflexive pronouns — возвратные местоимения.

Personal pronouns, то есть личные местоимения, обозначают человека или предмет. В предложении они могут быть подлежащим или дополнением. В роли подлежащего используются: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Например:

I am a student — Я студент.
You are my friend — Ты мой друг.
He is a teacher — Он учитель.
She is a doctor — Она врач.
It is a book — Это книга.
We are students — Мы студенты.
They are teachers — Они учителя.

Здесь местоимения стоят в начале предложения и обозначают человека или предмет, который выполняет действие. В английском he используется для мужчины, she — для женщины, а it — для животных, вещей, предметов или абстрактных понятий. Например: This is my phone. It is new — Это мой телефон. Он новый.

Личные местоимения, когда они выступают в роли дополнения, изменяют свою форму: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Например:

She helps me — Она помогает мне.
I know him — Я его знаю.
We love her — Мы её любим.
Teacher asked us — Учитель спросил нас.
I saw them yesterday — Я их видел вчера.

Здесь me, him, her, us, them не выполняют действие, наоборот, действие направлено на них. Поэтому I saw he — это неправильно, правильно: I saw him. She called I также неправильно, правильно: She called me.

Притяжательные прилагательные и притяжательные местоимения, то есть местоимения, указывающие на принадлежность, показывают, кому принадлежит что-то. В английском языке есть два вида выражения принадлежности. Первый используется вместе с существительным: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Например:

my book — моя книга,
your pen — твоя ручка,
his car — его машина,
her bag — её сумка,
our school — наша школа,
their house — их дом.

После этих слов обязательно следует существительное. Например: This is my book — Это моя книга. Her English is good — Её английский хороший. Their teacher is very kind — Их учитель очень добрый.

Второй вид используется самостоятельно вместо существительного: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Например:

This book is mine — Эта книга моя.
That pen is yours — Та ручка твоя.
This car is his — Эта машина его.
The red bag is hers — Эта красная сумка её.
This classroom is ours — Этот класс наш.
That house is theirs — Тот дом их.

Здесь после местоимения существительное не следует, так как оно уже было упомянуто или понятно из контекста. Например, This is my book. That is yours — Это моя книга. То — твоя. В этом предложении слово yours используется вместо your book.

Возвратные местоимения, то есть о́злик о́лмосхлари, указывают на то, что действие возвращается к субъекту. Они: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Например:

I taught myself English — Я сам выучил английский.
She looked at herself in the mirror — Она посмотрела на себя в зеркало.
He hurt himself — Он поранил себя.
We prepared ourselves for the exam — Мы подготовили себя к экзамену.
They introduced themselves — Они представились.

Возвратные местоимения означают «сам, сама, сами». Эти местоимения особенно показывают, что действие направлено не на другого человека, а именно на самого исполнителя.

Возвратные местоимения иногда также используются для подчеркивания. Например:

I did it myself — Я сделал это сам.

В этом предложении имеется в виду «не кто-то другой, а именно я сделал».

The director himself came to the meeting — Сам директор пришёл на встречу.
She herself cooked the dinner — Ужин приготовила она сама.

В таких случаях возвратное местоимение усиливает действие и придаёт предложению более уверенный тон.

Следующие примеры помогут лучше понять разницу между местоимениями:

I am a student — здесь I является личным местоимением, выполняющим роль подлежащего.
Teacher helped me — здесь me является личным местоимением, выполняющим роль дополнения.
This is my notebook — здесь my указывает на принадлежность и за ним следует существительное.
This notebook is mine — здесь mine используется самостоятельно в значении «мой». 
I bought it myself — здесь myself используется в значении «сам».

В заключение, местоимения в английском языке заменяют существительные, делая речь более естественной и избегая повторов. Personal pronouns обозначают человека или предмет: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Их формы дополнений: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Possessive adjectives показывают, кому принадлежит предмет, вместе с существительным: my book, your pen, his car, her bag. Possessive pronouns же используются самостоятельно в значении «мой, твой, его, её, наш, их»: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Reflexive pronouns означают «сам, сама, сами»: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Правильное использование этих местоимений очень важно для того, чтобы говорить на английском языке свободно, точно и красиво.
grammar_rules_kk:
Inglis tilinde pronoun, yaǵnıy almasıq, atlıqtıń ornına qollanılatuǵın sózdir. Mısalı, hár saparı Ali, Ali, Ali dep qaytalawdıń ornına biz he deymiz. This is Ali. Ali is my friend. Ali is a student dewdiń ornına tábiyiyirek etip: This is Ali. He is my friend. He is a student deymiz. Demek, almasıqlar gápti qısqaraq, jaqsıraq hám qaytalawlarsız etiw ushın kerek. Inglis tilinde almasıqlar júdá áhmiyetli, sebebi olar gápte kim haqqında aytılıp atırǵanın, zat kimge tiyisli ekenin yamasa is-háreket kimniń ózine baǵdarlanǵanın bildiredi. Eń kóp qollanılatuǵın almasıq túrleri: personal pronouns — betlik almasıqlar, possessive pronouns / possessive adjectives — iyelik almasıqlar hám reflexive pronouns — ózlik almasıqlar.

Personal pronouns, yaǵnıy betlik almasıqlar, shaxs yamasa zattı bildirip atır. Olar gápte baslawısh yamasa tolıqlawısh bolıp keliwi múmkin. Baslawısh bolıp kelgende: I, you, he, she, it, we, they qollanıladı. Mısalı:

I am a student — Men studentpen.
You are my friend — Sen meniń dosımsań.
He is a teacher — Ol (er adam) oqıtıwshı.
She is a doctor — Ol (hayal adam) shıpaker.
It is a book — Bul kitap.
We are students — Biz studentlermiz.
They are teachers — Olar oqıtıwshılar.

Bul jerde almasıqlar gáptiń basında kelip, is-háreketti orınlap atırǵan adamdı yamasa zattı bildirip atır. Inglis tilinde he er adam ushın, she hayal adam ushın, al it haywan, zat, buyım yamasa abstrakt túsinikler ushın qollanıladı. Mısalı: This is my phone. It is new — Bul meniń telefonım. Ol jańa.

Betlik almasıqlar gápte tolıqlawısh bolıp kelgende şekli ózgeredi: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Mısalı:

She helps me — U menga yardım beredi.
I know him — Men uni taniyman.
We love her — Biz uni jaqsı köreminiz.
Teacher asked us — Oqıtıwshı bizden soradı.
I saw them yesterday — Men ularni keshe kördim.

Bul jerde me, him, her, us, them is-háreketti bajarmaydı, aksinsha is-háreket ularga baǵdarlanǵan boladı. Sonlıqtan I saw he deyish notoǵrı, toǵrısı: I saw him. She called I ham notoǵrı, toǵrısı: She called me.

Possessive adjectives hám possessive pronouns, yaǵnıy iyelikni bildirip atırǵan almasıqlar, biror zat kimge tiyisli ekenin körsetedi. Inglis tilinde iyelikni bildiriwdiń eki köri bar. Biri ot menen birge qollanıladı: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Mısalı:

my book — meniń kitapım,
your pen — seniń ruchkang,
his car — uning mashinası,
her bag — uning sumkası,
our school — bizniń mektebimiz,
their house — olardıń uyı.

Bul sózlerden keyin albatta ot kelip atır. Mısalı: This is my book — Bul meniń kitapım. Her English is good — Uning ingliz tili jaqsı. Their teacher is very kind — Olardıń oqıtıwshısı júdá mehriban.

Ikkinci köri bolsa otning ornına mustaqıl qollanıladı: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Mısalı:

This book is mine — Bul kitap menińki.
That pen is yours — Ana u ruchka senińki.
This car is his — Bul mashina uningki.
The red bag is hers — Qızıl sumka uningki.
This classroom is ours — Bul sinfxona bizniki.
That house is theirs — Ana u uy olarnıńki.

Bul jerde almasıqdan keyin ot kelmeydi, sebebi ot avval aytilǵan yamasa mańadan túsinilgen boladı. Mısalı, This is my book. That is yours — Bul meniń kitapım. Ana unisi senińki. Bul gápte yours sózi your book ornına qollanılǵan.

Reflexive pronouns, yaǵnıy ózlik almasıqlar, is-háreket bajarıwshınıń ózine qaytısın bildirip atır. Olar: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Mısalı:

I taught myself English — Men ingliz tilinı ózim óyrendim.
She looked at herself in the mirror — U oynada ózine qaradı.
He hurt himself — U ózini jarohatlap aldı.
We prepared ourselves for the exam — Biz imtihonga ózimizdi tayyorladıq.
They introduced themselves — Olar ózlerin tanıstırdı.

Ózlik almasıqlar “ózim, ózing, ózi, ózimiz, ózleri” mańosın beredi. Bul almasıqlar ayniqsa is-háreket basqa adamğa emes, aynan bajarıwshınıń ózine baǵdarlanǵanın körsetedi.

Ózlik almasıqlar ba’zan ta’kidlaw ushın ham qollanıladı. Mısalı:

I did it myself — Men buni ózim qıldım.

Bul gápte “başqa adam emes, aynan men qıldım” degan mańo bar.

The director himself came to the meeting — Direktorning ózi majlisqa keldi.
She herself cooked the dinner — Ovqatnı uning ózi pışırdı.

Bunday holatda ózlik almasıq is-háreketni kúshtıraqtı ta’kidlaydı hám gápqa ishonçlıraq ohang beredi.

Quyıdıqı mısallar almasıqların farqın jaqsıraq túsinwi ushın kömek beredi:

I am a student — bul jerde I kishilik almasıq, ega vazifasında kelgen.
Teacher helped me — bul jerde me kishilik almasıq, tolıqlawısh vazifasında kelgen.
This is my notebook — bul jerde my iyelikni bildirip atır hám undan keyin ot kelgen.
This notebook is mine — bul jerde mine “menińki” degan mańoda mustaqıl qollanılǵan.
I bought it myself — bul jerde myself “ózim” degan mańoda qollanılǵan.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, pronouns inglis tilinde atlıqtıń ornına kelip, gápni takrorsız hám tabiıy etedi. Personal pronouns shaxs yamasa zattı bildirip: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Olardıń tolıqlawısh şekilleri: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Possessive adjectives narsa kimge tiyisli ekenin at menen birge kórsatadı: my book, your pen, his car, her bag. Possessive pronouns esa “meniki, seniki, uniki, bizniki, ularniki” ma’nosında mustaqıl qollanıladı: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Reflexive pronouns esa “o‘zim, o‘zing, o‘zi, o‘zimiz, o‘zlari” ma’nosını bildirip: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Bul almasıqların toǵrı qollanılıwı inglis tilinde ravon, anıq hám chiroylı gápiriw ushın juda muhim.
reading_passage:
This week I learned about a classroom lost-and-found table. Our class used a realistic situation from the language department office.

Several notebooks, pens, headphones and water bottles are waiting for their owners. Amina recognizes her blue notebook but the black headphones are not hers.

A label inside one bag shows the owner’s name. Students are encouraged to check their own belongings before taking anything.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “Amina brings a tablet. It belongs to her, and she sets it up herself.” Most of the lost items are returned to the correct students that afternoon.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Amina explains the main idea to Tom and supports the answer with information from the text.

The final task asks readers to connect the topic with their own experience. They should explain one idea in their own words and then use the lesson grammar in a new sentence about a classroom lost-and-found table.

reading_vocabulary.example: The lesson uses “headphones” in the context of a classroom lost-and-found table.

reading_vocabulary.example: The lesson uses “recognize” in the context of a classroom lost-and-found table.

reading_vocabulary.example: The lesson uses “return” in the context of a classroom lost-and-found table.

listening_transcript:
Amina: Tom, I was thinking about our lesson on a classroom lost-and-found table.
Tom: Me too. We have to identify who owns several classroom items, so the details matter.
Amina: I wrote down the first point. Tell me if this is right.
Tom: Tom finds a tablet on the teacher’s desk.
Amina: What did you write for the next point?
Tom: Amina says the tablet belongs to her roommate.
Amina: I nearly missed another detail.
Tom: Tom points to a red umbrella and asks whether it is hers.
Amina: Yes, and there is one more fact we should not forget.
Tom: Amina checks the name tag and realizes the umbrella belongs to another student.
Amina: Let’s check the grammar before we finish.
Tom: For example: Amina brings a tablet. It belongs to her, and she sets it up herself.
Amina: Great. What happened in the end?
Tom: They leave the remaining items at the office for their owners.

help a friend who is worried about tomorrow’s test
decide which software a student really needs
give advice while reviewing a web design

grammar_rules:
Bu darsda siz ingliz tilida bitta narsa va ko‘p narsani aytishni, biror joyda nima borligini tasvirlashni va narsalarning qayerda joylashganini aytishni o‘rganasiz.

Siz do‘stingizga xonangizni, sinfxonangizni yoki ish stolingizni tasvirlayapsiz.

Masalan:

There is a book on the table.
Stol ustida bitta kitob bor.

There are two books on the table.
Stol ustida ikkita kitob bor.

There is a bag under the chair.
Stul tagida bitta sumka bor

Singular noun nima?

Singular noun — bitta odam, bitta hayvon yoki bitta narsa.

O‘zbekcha: birlikdagi ot

Masalan:

a book — bitta kitob
a pen — bitta ruchka
a chair — bitta stul
a table — bitta stol
a phone — bitta telefon
a bag — bitta sumka
a student — bitta talaba

Singular noun oldidan ko‘pincha a yoki an ishlatiladi.

3. A / An qanday ishlatiladi?

Agar so‘z undosh tovush bilan boshlansa, a ishlatiladi.

a book

a pen

a table

grammar_rules_en:
In this lesson you will learn to talk about one thing and many things in English, to describe what there is in a place, and to say where things are.

You are describing your room, your classroom or your desk to a friend.

For example:

There is a book on the table.

There are two books on the table.

There is a bag under the chair.

What is a singular noun?

A singular noun is one person, one animal or one thing.

Uzbek: singular noun

For example:

a book — one book
a pen — one pen
a chair — one chair
a table — one table
a phone — one phone
a bag — one bag
a student — one student

A singular noun is often preceded by a or an.

3. How is A / An used?

If the word starts with a consonant sound, a is used.

a book

a pen

a table

a phone

If the word starts with a vowel sound, an is used.

an apple

an eraser

an umbrella

What is a plural noun?

A plural noun is two or more people, animals, or things.

Uzbek: plural noun

To form a plural, -s is usually added to the end of the word.

Singular | Plural
a book | books
a pen | pens
a chair | chairs
a table | tables
a phone | phones
a bag | bags
a student | students

Examples:

one book
two books

one pen
three pens

Words that add -es

If a word ends with s, sh, ch, x, or o, -es is often added.

Singular | Plural
box | boxes
watch | watches
class | classes
dish | dishes
tomato | tomatoes

Examples:

There is a box.
There is one box.

There are two boxes.
There are two boxes.

Words ending with -y

If a word ends with a consonant + y, the y is dropped and -ies is added.

Singular | Plural
city | cities
baby | babies
story | stories

Examples:

There is a city.
There is one city.

There are many cities.
There are many cities.

But if it ends with a vowel + y, only -s is added:

Singular | Plural
boy | boys
toy | toys
key | keys

Irregular plural nouns

Some nouns do not simply add -s in the plural. They change.

Singular | Plural
man | men
woman | women
child | children
person | people
foot | feet
tooth | teeth
mouse | mice

Examples:

There is a child in the room.
There is one child in the room.

There are children in the room.
There are children in the room.

What is There is / There are for?

If you want to say that there is something in a place, you use there is or there are in English.

In Uzbek:

There is a table in the room.
There are books on the table.
There is a bag under the chair.

In English:

There is a table in the room.
There are books on the table.
There is a bag under the chair.

When is There is used?

There is is used for one thing.

Examples:

There is a book on the table.
There is one book on the table.

There is a pen in the bag.
There is one pen in the bag.

There is a chair in the room.
There is one chair in the room.

There is an apple on the plate.
There is one apple on the plate.

When is There are used?

There are is used for plural things.

Examples:

There are books on the table.
There are books on the table.

There are pens in the bag.
There are pens in the bag.

There are chairs in the room.
There are chairs in the room.

There are students in the classroom.
There are students in the classroom.

11. The difference between There is and There are

One thing | Many things
There is a book. | There are books.
There is a pen. | There are pens.
There is a chair. | There are chairs.
There is a student. | There are students.
There is an apple. | There are apples.

Important rule:

There is — one thing.
There are — many things.

Prepositions in, on, under

Prepositions are used to say where something is located.

In

In — inside.

Examples:

There is a pen in the bag.
There is one pen in the bag.

There are books in the box.
There are books in the box.

There is a student in the classroom.
There is one student in the classroom.

On

On — on top of.

Examples:

There is a book on the table.
There is one book on the table.

There are pens on the desk.
There are pens on the desk.

There is a phone on the chair.
There is one phone on the chair.

Under

Under — underneath.

Examples:

There is a bag under the chair.
There is one bag under the chair.

There are shoes under the table.
There are shoes under the table.

There is a box under the bed.
There is one box under the bed.
grammar_rules_ru:
На этом уроке вы научитесь говорить по-английски об одном предмете и о многих предметах, описывать, что есть в каком-то месте, и говорить, где находятся вещи.

Вы описываете другу свою комнату, класс или рабочий стол.

Например:

There is a book on the table.
На столе одна книга.

There are two books on the table.
На столе две книги.

There is a bag under the chair.
Под стулом одна сумка.

Что такое singular noun?

Singular noun — один человек, одно животное или один предмет.

Узбекча: единственное число существительного

Например:

a book — одна книга
a pen — одна ручка
a chair — один стул
a table — один стол
a phone — один телефон
a bag — одна сумка
a student — один студент

Перед singular noun часто используется a или an.

3. Как используется A / An?

Если слово начинается с согласного звука, используется a.

a book
одна книга

a pen
одна ручка

a table
один стол

a phone
один телефон

Если слово начинается с гласного звука, используется an.

an apple
одно яблоко

an eraser
одный ластик

an umbrella
один зонт

Что такое plural noun?

Plural noun — два или более человека, животного или предмета.

Узбекча: множественное число существительного

Чтобы образовать множественное число, обычно добавляется -s в конце слова.

Единственное | Множественное
a book | books
a pen | pens
a chair | chairs
a table | tables
a phone | phones
a bag | bags
a student | students

Примеры:

one book — одна книга
two books — две книги

one pen — одна ручка
three pens — три ручки

Слова, к которым добавляется -es

Если слово заканчивается на s, sh, ch, x, o, обычно добавляется -es.

Единственное | Множественное
box | boxes
watch | watches
class | classes
dish | dishes
tomato | tomatoes

Примеры:

There is a box.
Есть одна коробка.

There are two boxes.
Есть две коробки.

Слова, заканчивающиеся на -y

Если слово заканчивается на согласную + y, y убирается и добавляется -ies.

Единственное | Множественное
city | cities
baby | babies
story | stories

Примеры:

There is a city.
Есть один город.

There are many cities.
Есть много городов.

Но если y стоит после гласной, добавляется только -s:

Единственное | Множественное
boy | boys
toy | toys
key | keys

Неправильные существительные во множественном числе

Некоторые существительные во множественном числе не получают простое -s. Они изменяются.

Единственное | Множественное
man | men
woman | women
child | children
person | people
foot | feet
tooth | teeth
mouse | mice

Примеры:

There is a child in the room.
В комнате есть один ребенок.

There are children in the room.
В комнате есть дети.

Зачем нужно There is / There are?

Если вы хотите сказать, что что-то есть в каком-то месте, в английском языке используется there is или there are.

На узбекском:

В комнате есть стол.
На столе есть книги.
Сумка стоит под стулом.

На английском:

There is a table in the room.
There are books on the table.
There is a bag under the chair.

Когда используется There is?

There is — используется для одного предмета.

Примеры:

There is a book on the table.
На столе одна книга.

There is a pen in the bag.
В сумке одна ручка.

There is a chair in the room.
В комнате один стул.

There is an apple on the plate.
На тарелке одно яблоко.

Когда используется There are?

There are — используется для множественного числа предметов.

Примеры:

There are books on the table.
На столе есть книги.

There are pens in the bag.
В сумке есть ручки.

There are chairs in the room.
В комнате есть стулья.

There are students in the classroom.
В классе есть студенты.

11. Разница между There is и There are

Одно предмет | Много предметов
There is a book. | There are books.
There is a pen. | There are pens.
There is a chair. | There are chairs.
There is a student. | There are students.
There is an apple. | There are apples.

Важное правило:

There is — для одного предмета.
There are — для множества предметов.

Предлоги in, on, under

Предлоги используются для указания, где находится предмет.

In

In — внутри.

Примеры:

There is a pen in the bag.
В сумке одна ручка.

There are books in the box.
В коробке есть книги.

There is a student in the classroom.
В классе есть один студент.

On

On — на.

Примеры:

There is a book on the table.
На столе одна книга.

There are pens on the desk.
На парте есть ручки.

There is a phone on the chair.
На стуле один телефон.

Under

Under — под.

Примеры:

There is a bag under the chair.
Под стулом одна сумка.

There are shoes under the table.
Под столом есть обувь.

There is a box under the bed.
Под кроватью одна коробка.

reading_passage:
In a short student interview, Eva explains what the class learned about organising a study desk in a quiet dormitory room.

There is one laptop in the centre of the desk and two notebooks beside it. A lamp stands behind the laptop so the screen is easier to read at night.

Cables are kept in a small box under the desk. Books that are used every day are placed on the shelf above the desk.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “There is a notebook on the desk, and there are two cables under the monitor.” The organised desk gives Eva more space and helps her find things quickly.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Eva explains the main idea to Noah and supports the answer with information from the text.

listening_transcript:
Eva: Hi Noah. I’m calling about the lesson on organising a study desk.
Noah: Perfect timing. I’m reviewing how to help a roommate reorganise a crowded desk.
Eva: Can you remind me of the first detail?

Eva: Thanks. What comes after that?

Eva: Was there another important point?

Eva: I need one last detail for my notes.
Noah: Noah suggests keeping the phone away from the study area.

grammar_rules:
Noun (ot) – sanaladigan / sanalmaydigan (Countable vs Uncountable nouns)

Ingliz tilida noun, ya’ni ot, odam, narsa, joy, hayvon, fikr yoki tushunchaning nomini bildiradi: student, book, water, idea, school, happiness. Otlar ingliz tilida ikki katta guruhga bo‘linadi: countable nouns va uncountable nouns.

Countable nouns — bu sanash mumkin bo‘lgan otlar. Ya’ni ularning bittasini, ikkitasini, uchtasini alohida sanay olamiz. Masalan:

one book,
two books,
three students,
five apples.

Bunday otlarning singular va plural shakli bo‘ladi. Bitta bo‘lsa oldidan ko‘pincha a/an ishlatiladi: a book, an apple, a student. Ko‘plikda esa odatda -s / -es qo‘shiladi: books, apples, boxes, buses. Masalan:

I have a book — “Menda bitta kitob bor”.
She bought three apples — “U uchta olma sotib oldi”.

Bu yerda book va apple sanaladi, chunki ularni donalab hisoblash mumkin.

Uncountable nouns esa sanab bo‘lmaydigan otlardir. Ular odatda suyuqlik, kukun, modda, ovqat nomlari, umumiy tushuncha yoki hissiyotlarni bildiradi. Masalan:

water, milk, rice, sugar, bread, money, information, advice, knowledge, love, happiness.

Biz ingliz tilida one water yoki two milks demaymiz, chunki suv yoki sutni o‘zini donalab sanamaymiz. Ularni o‘lchov orqali aytamiz:

a glass of water — bir stakan suv,
two bottles of milk — ikki butilka sut,
a kilo of rice — bir kilo guruch,
a piece of advice — bitta maslahat.

Demak, uncountable noun bilan ishlaganda narsaning o‘zini emas, uning miqdorini bildiruvchi so‘zdan foydalanamiz. Masalan:

I drink water every day — “Men har kuni suv ichaman”.
She gave me some useful advice — “U menga foydali maslahat berdi”.

Bu gaplarda water va advice ko‘plik shaklida kelmaydi.

Countable va uncountable otlarni farqlashda eng oson yo‘l — “Buni donalab sanay olamanmi?” deb o‘zingizga savol berish. Agar “ha” bo‘lsa, u countable noun: pen, chair, banana, car, lesson. Agar “yo‘q, lekin miqdorini o‘lchash mumkin” bo‘lsa, u uncountable noun: tea, coffee, flour, meat, homework, information. Masalan, chair sanaladi: one chair, two chairs. Lekin furniture sanalmaydi. O‘zbek tilida “mebellar” deyishimiz mumkin, ammo ingliz tilida furnituresdemaymiz. To‘g‘ri shakl: some furniture yoki two pieces of furniture. Xuddi shuningdek, homework ham sanalmaydi. I have many homeworks noto‘g‘ri. To‘g‘risi: I have a lot of homework yoki I have two homework tasks.

Bu mavzuda yana bir muhim farq bor: countable nouns bilan many, few, a few ishlatiladi; uncountable nouns bilan esa much, little, a little ishlatiladi. Masalan:

many books — ko‘p kitoblar,
few students — kam talabalar,
a few questions — bir nechta savollar.

Lekin:

much water — ko‘p suv,
little time — oz vaqt,
a little sugar — ozgina shakar.

Ikkalasiga ham mos keladigan umumiy so‘zlar ham bor: some, any, a lot of, plenty of. Masalan: some books ham bo‘ladi, some water ham bo‘ladi. A lot of students ham to‘g‘ri, a lot of money ham to‘g‘ri.

Ba’zi otlar esa vaziyatga qarab countable ham, uncountable ham bo‘lishi mumkin. Masalan, chicken so‘zi “tovuq go‘shti” ma’nosida sanalmaydi: I ate chicken for lunch — “Tushlikda tovuq go‘shti yedim”. Lekin “tovuq” degan hayvon ma’nosida sanaladi: There are three chickens in the yard — “Hovlida uchta tovuq bor”. Paper ham shunday: agar “qog‘oz materiali” bo‘lsa sanalmaydi: I need some paper. Agar “maqola, hujjat, gazeta” ma’nosida bo‘lsa sanaladi: I read two papers. Demak, ingliz tilida otning sanalishi faqat so‘zning o‘ziga emas, gapdagi ma’nosiga ham bog‘liq bo‘lishi mumkin.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, countable nouns — sanash mumkin bo‘lgan otlar: a book, two books, an apple, five apples. Uncountable nouns — donalab sanalmaydigan, lekin miqdor bilan ifodalanadigan otlar: water, rice, money, information, advice. Countable otlarda birlik va ko‘plik shakli bor, uncountable otlar esa odatda ko‘plikka o‘tmaydi va oldidan a/anolmaydi. Shuning uchun ingliz tilida an information, advices, many money, three breads kabi shakllar noto‘g‘ri hisoblanadi. To‘g‘ri variantlar: some information, a piece of advice, much money, three pieces of bread. Bu mavzuni yaxshi tushunish ingliz tilida tabiiyroq gapirish va xatolarsiz yozish uchun juda muhim.
grammar_rules_en:
Noun (noun) – countable / uncountable (Countable vs Uncountable nouns)

In English, a noun names a person, thing, place, animal, idea or concept: student, book, water, idea, school, happiness. Nouns in English fall into two big groups: countable nouns and uncountable nouns.

Countable nouns are nouns we can count. That means we can count them one by one: one, two, three. For example:

one book,
two books,
three students,
five apples.

These nouns have a singular and a plural form. In the singular they usually take a/an: a book, an apple, a student. In the plural we usually add -s / -es: books, apples, boxes, buses. For example:

I have a book.
She bought three apples.

Here book and apple are countable, because we can count them one by one.

Uncountable nouns are nouns we cannot count. They usually name liquids, powders, substances, foods, general ideas or feelings. For example:

water, milk, rice, sugar, bread, money, information, advice, knowledge, love, happiness.

We do not say one water or two milks in English, because we do not count water or milk individually. We express them through measurement:

a glass of water — a glass of water,
two bottles of milk — two bottles of milk,
a kilo of rice — a kilo of rice,
a piece of advice — a piece of advice.

Thus, when working with uncountable nouns, we use words that indicate quantity rather than the item itself. For example:

I drink water every day.
She gave me some useful advice.

In these sentences, water and advice do not come in plural form.

The easiest way to distinguish between countable and uncountable nouns is to ask yourself, 'Can I count this individually?' If the answer is 'yes', it is a countable noun: pen, chair, banana, car, lesson. If the answer is 'no, but it can be measured', it is an uncountable noun: tea, coffee, flour, meat, homework, information. For example, chair is countable: one chair, two chairs. But furniture is uncountable. We can say 'mebellar' in Uzbek, but in English we do not say 'furnitures'. The correct form is: some furniture or two pieces of furniture. Similarly, homework is also uncountable. I have many homeworks is incorrect. The correct form is: I have a lot of homework or I have two homework tasks.

There is another important distinction in this topic: with countable nouns we use many, few, a few; with uncountable nouns we use much, little, a little. For example:

many books — many books,
few students — few students,
a few questions — a few questions.

But:

much water — much water,
little time — little time,
a little sugar — a little sugar.

There are also general words that fit both: some, any, a lot of, plenty of. For example: some books is correct, and some water is also correct. A lot of students is correct, and a lot of money is also correct.

Some nouns can be both countable and uncountable depending on the context. For example, the word chicken is uncountable when it means 'chicken meat': I ate chicken for lunch. But it is countable when it means 'the animal': There are three chickens in the yard. Paper is similar: if it means 'paper material', it is uncountable: I need some paper. If it means 'article, document, newspaper', it is countable: I read two papers. Thus, in English, whether a noun is countable can depend not only on the word itself but also on its meaning in the sentence.

In conclusion, countable nouns are nouns we can count: a book, two books, an apple, five apples. Uncountable nouns are nouns that cannot be counted individually but are expressed in terms of quantity: water, rice, money, information, advice. Countable nouns have singular and plural forms, while uncountable nouns usually do not take plural forms and do not take a/an before them. Therefore, forms like an information, advices, many money, three breads are considered incorrect in English. The correct variants are: some information, a piece of advice, much money, three pieces of bread. Understanding this topic well is very important for speaking and writing in English more naturally and without mistakes.
grammar_rules_ru:
Существительное (noun) – исчисляемые / неисчисляемые (Countable vs Uncountable nouns)

В английском языке существительное (noun) обозначает человека, предмет, место, животное, мысль или понятие: student, book, water, idea, school, happiness. Существительные в английском языке делятся на две большие группы: countable nouns и uncountable nouns.

Исчисляемые существительные (Countable nouns) — это существительные, которые можно посчитать. То есть их можно считать по отдельности: одну, две, три. Например:

one book,
two books,
three students,
five apples.

У таких существительных есть форма единственного и множественного числа. В единственном числе перед ними обычно ставится a/an: a book, an apple, a student. Во множественном числе обычно добавляется -s / -es: books, apples, boxes, buses. Например:

I have a book — «У меня есть книга». 
She bought three apples — «Она купила три яблока».

Здесь book и apple исчисляемые, потому что их можно посчитать поштучно.

Неисчисляемые существительные (Uncountable nouns) — это существительные, которые нельзя посчитать. Обычно они обозначают жидкости, порошки, вещества, продукты, общие понятия или чувства. Например:

water, milk, rice, sugar, bread, money, information, advice, knowledge, love, happiness.

В английском языке мы не говорим one water или two milks, потому что воду или молоко нельзя считать поштучно. Мы выражаем их через измерение:

a glass of water — один стакан воды,
two bottles of milk — две бутылки молока,
a kilo of rice — один килограмм риса,
a piece of advice — один совет.

Таким образом, при работе с неисчисляемыми существительными мы используем слово, обозначающее количество, а не само существительное. Например:

I drink water every day — «Я пью воду каждый день». 
She gave me some useful advice — «Она дала мне несколько полезных советов».

В этих предложениях water и advice не имеют формы множественного числа.

Самый простой способ различить исчисляемые и неисчисляемые существительные — задать себе вопрос: «Могу ли я посчитать это поштучно?» Если ответ «да», то это countable noun: pen, chair, banana, car, lesson. Если ответ «нет, но можно измерить количество», то это uncountable noun: tea, coffee, flour, meat, homework, information. Например, chair исчисляется: one chair, two chairs. Но furniture не исчисляется. В узбекском языке мы можем сказать «mebellar», но в английском языке furniture не существует во множественном числе. Правильная форма: some furniture или two pieces of furniture. Точно так же homework также не исчисляется. I have many homeworks — это неправильно. Правильно: I have a lot of homework или I have two homework tasks.

В этой теме есть еще одно важное различие: с исчисляемыми существительными используются many, few, a few; с неисчисляемыми существительными — much, little, a little. Например:

many books — много книг,
few students — мало студентов,
a few questions — несколько вопросов.

Но:

much water — много воды,
little time — мало времени,
a little sugar — немного сахара.

Существуют также общие слова, которые подходят для обоих типов: some, any, a lot of, plenty of. Например: some books также возможно, some water также возможно. A lot of students также правильно, a lot of money также правильно.

Некоторые существительные могут быть как исчисляемыми, так и неисчисляемыми в зависимости от контекста. Например, слово chicken в значении «куриное мясо» не исчисляется: I ate chicken for lunch — «Я ел куриное мясо на обед». Но в значении «курица» оно исчисляется: There are three chickens in the yard — «Во дворе три курицы». Paper также таково: если это «материал для бумаги», то оно не исчисляется: I need some paper. Если это «статья, документ, газета», то оно исчисляется: I read two papers. Таким образом, в английском языке исчисляемость существительного может зависеть не только от самого слова, но и от его значения в предложении.

В заключение, исчисляемые существительные — это те, которые можно посчитать: a book, two books, an apple, five apples. Неисчисляемые существительные — это те, которые нельзя считать поштучно, но которые выражаются количественно: water, rice, money, information, advice. У исчисляемых существительных есть форма единственного и множественного числа, тогда как неисчисляемые существительные обычно не имеют множественного числа и не могут иметь перед собой a/an. Поэтому в английском языке формы an information, advices, many money, three breads считаются неправильными. Правильные варианты: some information, a piece of advice, much money, three pieces of bread. Понимание этой темы очень важно для того, чтобы говорить на английском более естественно и писать без ошибок.

The student magazine has a new feature on choosing a computer for university work. It begins with a situation from an electronics shop near campus.

The student needs a laptop with enough memory for documents and video calls. The salesperson explains that storage space is measured in gigabytes.

There are several lightweight models but only a little information about battery life on the display cards. The student has some money saved but does not want to buy unnecessary accessories.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “There are two files and some useful information on the screen.” After comparing the options, Lena chooses a simple laptop with good battery life.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Lena explains the main idea to Sam and supports the answer with information from the text.
